summary.short: Interim final rule amending the Export Administration Regulations to revise export controls on advanced computing integrated circuits, computer commodities containing them, and supercomputers, plus related end-use and U.S.-person rules. Binds exporters and foreign manufacturers; effective November 17, 2023.
summary.long: Interim final rule, published October 25, 2023 in the Federal Register, amending the Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR parts 732 to 774) to revise the October 7, 2022 controls on advanced computing integrated circuits, computer commodities containing them, and supercomputers. It replaces the 3A090 parameters with total processing performance and performance density thresholds, adds License Exception Notified Advanced Computing (NAC) with prior notification for exports to Macau and Country Group D:5, and adds .z items paragraphs to nine ECCNs. Regional stability license requirements are extended to destinations in Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5 not also in A:5 or A:6, with presumption-of-approval or presumption-of-denial license review policies. The rule broadens the advanced computing foreign direct product rule and the section 744.23 end-use controls to entities headquartered in Macau or Country Group D:5, expands the section 744.6 U.S.-person activity controls, requires .z classification in export filings and commercial invoices, and adds five red flags. It is effective November 17, 2023, except one amendatory instruction effective through January 1, 2026; comments are due December 18, 2023.

notes: This annotation covers part 1 of 3 only (cover, Summary, Background, public comments and Section C through C.10 as provided). Relations and entities come only from this part. The text is an interim final rule with a request for comments. Several provisions say 'this SME IFR' inside this AC/S IFR's text, which refers to the concurrently published rule; those redesignations are not annotated here. Section status is set to not_applicable only because the schema requires the field; entries are present above. Part 2 of 3 only: relations and entities cover provisions in this part (sections 11 to 12 and the amendments to Parts 732 to 774 of the EAR). Target instrument IDs are empty because no registry match was checked for the cited instruments. The text states that the TGLs in Supplement No. 1 to Part 736 expire on December 31, 2025. Minor text issues: Supplement No. 1 to Part 740 refers to Country Groups A:5 or A6 (A6 for A:6), and Section 744.6(d)(1)(ii) contains the stray word Tand. The AMD entry heading in Supplement No. 7 is line-broken in the source, so the entity name is taken from the facility address lines. Part 3 of 3 covers the Category 5 Part 2 ECCN lists (5A002, 5A004, 5A992, 5B002, 5D002, 5D992, 5E002, 5E992), ECCNs 9A004 and 9A515, and Amendment 39 to Supplement No. 6 to Part 774. The operative content is the control lists and license-exception entries, which are not coded here. No named firms or designated public bodies appear. NASA, the James Webb Space Telescope and the International Space Station are mentioned only as items or program references; the signing Assistant Secretary is not recorded as an entity. Legal basis and the amending instruction for the rule as a whole fall in parts 1 and 2. The Federal Register page header and OCR artifacts ('lotter on DSK11XQN23PROD') are not substantive text.
